Row.Text: The Qajar commander kneels before his father’s enshrined skull, silently asking for guidance. At home, the Zand tribe and other claimants to Iran’s throne plot their uprisings, and the great powers of the world constantly conspire for Iran’s riches. How can he, whose line stems not from the great Persian shahs but from the tribal people on civilization’s edge, secure Qajar’s hold on Iran?
The skull is silent, but its eye sockets convey a message: to give ground is death.
The skull waits silently. So shall the Qajar be patient.
